subject: maths
question: A seasoned marathoner, known for his steady pace, usually runs the first half of a race at 8 km/hr and the second half at 6 km/hr. However, due to fatigue and other factors, his overall speed drops by 30%. How long will it take him to complete a 120 km marathon under these reduced-speed conditions?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Average speed for equal distances = (2ab) ÷ (a + b)

= (2 × 8 × 6) ÷ (8 + 6) = 96 ÷ 14 = 48/7 km/hr

Reduced speed = 70% of (48/7) = (48/7) × 0.7 = 33.6/7 = 4.8 km/hr

Time = Distance ÷ Speed = 120 ÷ 4.8

= 25 hours

**∴ Answer = 25 hours**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance = 120 km

First half speed = 8 km/hr, Second half speed = 6 km/hr

Speed reduced by 30%

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed, Average speed for equal distances = (2ab) ÷ (a + b)

**Calculation:**

⇒ First half distance = 60 km, Second half = 60 km

⇒ Time for first half = 60 ÷ 8 = 7.5 hr

⇒ Time for second half = 60 ÷ 6 = 10 hr

⇒ Total time (normal) = 17.5 hr

⇒ Average speed = 120 ÷ 17.5 = 48/7 km/hr

⇒ Reduced speed = 70% of 48/7 = 4.8 km/hr

⇒ Time = 120 ÷ 4.8 = 25 hr

**∴ The correct answer is 25 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Distance)

Average speed = (2ab) ÷ (a + b) when distances are equal.

Percentage Decrease

New value = Original × (1 − decrease%). Here multiply by 0.7.

Speed-Time Relation

Speed and time are inversely proportional for fixed distance.
